content.text: I fixed the parser, but nothing is committed yet. **What broke:** In today's run, Step 3 failed when it tried to read the OpenCode Zen pricing page. That page now shows a sale price as `Mistral Large 4 (50% off)$1.36 $0.68…`. The parser read the crossed-out old price and the new price together as one value, `"$1.36 $0.68"`, and refused it. So the run kept yesterday's Zen pricing file and exited with code 1. Because of that, the mapping and data commits, the site build and the deploy were all skipped. Copilot, OpenCode Go and ClinePass pricing, the benchmark data and the scoring all finished fine. **Fix** in [src/opencode-zen/parser.ts](src/opencode-zen/parser.ts): - The parser now ignores crossed-out text (`` and `` tags) along with footnote markers, so a sale cell reads as the current price. - It removes a `(N% off)` suffix from the model name, so the model keeps the name `Mistral Large 4`. The discount is saved in `notes` as "Promotional pricing (50% off)." instead. I tested it on today's live page: all 103 rows parse, and Mistral Large 4 comes out at $0.68 input, $2.09 output and $0.07 cached read. Typecheck, lint and format all pass. I didn't run the full `npm start`, because it rewrites the files under `data/` and could start the local parser-repair agent. **Not causing the failure, but worth knowing:** - 47 models are skipped for "incomplete benchmark data", including the GPT 5 and 6 models and every Claude model. Only 75 candidates got scored. Benchmark data comes from Artificial Analysis on the free tier (`tier: free`), which may now leave some fields out. That's worth checking if the rankings look thin. - OpenCode Go has some "no matching row in: requests" warnings for the variants split by context length (GPT 6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5). Should I commit and push this so tomorrow's scheduled run picks it up, or would you rather start the workflow manually after pushing?
